title: You can sit in church every Sunday…
paragraphs:
You can sit in church every Sunday…
smile, sing, serve…
and still not know God.

That tension right there?
That’s where this message begins.

Because this is not about attendance.
This is about intimacy.

There’s a quiet danger that doesn’t shout.
It doesn’t scandalize headlines.
It hides in routine.

You raise your hands on cue.
You know when to say “Amen.”
You can finish the pastor’s verses before he does.

But when the music fades…
when the crowd goes home…
when it’s just you and your thoughts—
God feels distant.

Not absent in theory.
But absent in experience.
Jesus confronted this exact reality.

“These people honor Me with their lips,
but their hearts are far from Me.” — Matthew 15:8
Read that again.

Not rebels.
Not atheists.
Not outsiders.
Church people.

People who looked right…
but loved wrong.

You can master the language of faith
and still be a stranger to the God you speak about.

You can quote Scripture
and still resist surrender.

You can serve in ministry
and still protect secret sin.
This is the tragedy:

Being close to church…
but far from Christ.
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable.

Because many don’t walk away from God—
they sit near Him… without ever truly coming to Him.

They trade relationship for routine.
Conviction for comfort.
Surrender for control.

And slowly, subtly—
their heart drifts.

Not in one dramatic moment.
But in a thousand small compromises.
But listen, kapatid… don’t miss this.

This is not a message of condemnation.
This is a wake-up call wrapped in grace.

Because the very fact that this stirs something in you—
that uneasy feeling, that quiet conviction—
That’s not rejection.
That’s invitation.
God has never been impressed with perfect attendance.
From Genesis to Revelation, He’s after one thing:
Your heart.

Not your performance.
Not your image.
Not your reputation.
Your heart.

“You will seek Me and find Me
when you seek Me with all your heart.” — Jeremiah 29:13
And here’s the Gospel—the turning point, the lifeline, the fire in the darkness:
You don’t have to fix yourself first.

You don’t have to pretend.
You don’t have to clean up before you come close.

Jesus didn’t die for your polished version.
He died for your real one.

Broken.
Conflicted.
Hiding.

“I am the way, and the truth, and the life.
No one comes to the Father except through Me.” — John 14:6

Not through church attendance.
Not through good works.
Not through religious effort.
Through Jesus alone.
This is where everything changes.

Because knowing God is not about proximity to religion—
it’s about surrender to a Person.
And His name is Jesus.
So what does it actually look like to know Him?

It looks like repentance—
not just saying sorry, but turning around.

It looks like obedience—
not perfection, but direction.

It looks like hunger—
a desire for Him that goes beyond Sunday.

It looks like intimacy—
talking to Him, walking with Him, trusting Him in the quiet places.
And yes… it will cost you something.

Your pride.
Your hidden sins.
Your need to stay in control.
But what you gain?
Everything.

Forgiveness that is complete.
Grace that is undeserved.
A relationship that is alive.
Maybe you’ve been in church for years.
Maybe you know all the right things.

But deep down…
you know something is missing.
This is your moment.
Not to try harder.
But to come closer.
Right now, you can pray.

Not a performance prayer.
Not a memorized script.
Just real.

“Lord, I don’t want to just go through the motions anymore.
I want to know You.
Forgive me. Change me. Lead me.
I surrender my life to You.”
And He will meet you there.

Not with shame.
Not with rejection.
But with open arms.
Because that’s who Jesus is.

So don’t settle for being near the things of God
and missing the heart of God.
Don’t trade relationship for routine.
Don’t let familiarity replace fire.
Come back.
Not to religion.
But to Jesus.
Start a conversation.

Because someone out there is sitting in a pew…
feeling exactly this…
and waiting for a wake-up call.

From ritual to relationship.
From distance to intimacy.
From religion to redemption.
